2_Introduction: The PSCs displayed a significantly enhanced PCE of 16.001%, with VOC of 1.0028 V, JSC of 19.958 mA/cm², and FF of 79.954%. Then, perovskite precursor solution (1.73 mol/L) was prepared at the stoichiometric ratio of Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79PbI2.9Br0.1. The perovskite solution was deposited on the substrate by two consecutive spin-coating steps of 1000 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 30 s, respectively. At the last 6 s, 160 µL of chlorobenzene solution was dropped on the perovskite. Afterwards, the perovskite film was annealed at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The perovskite layer, formulated as Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁₆FA₀.₇₉PbI₂.₉Br₀.₁, leverages a carefully tuned A-site cation mixture to optimize the Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98), suppress phase segregation, and mitigate halide vacancy–mediated ion migration—particularly by incorporating Cs⁺ for lattice stiffening and FA⁺ for thermal stability, while MA⁺ enhances crystallinity kinetics without compromising phase purity; the 1.73 mol/L precursor concentration, combined with the two-step spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/10 s for wet-film formation followed by 5000 rpm/30 s for rapid solvent extraction), enables controlled nucleation density and grain coalescence, whereas the precisely timed antisolvent quenching at the final 6 s with 160 µL chlorobenzene arrests intermediate solvate phases (e.g., δ-FAPbI₃) and promotes direct transition to the photoactive α-phase, and the subsequent 110 °C/25 min annealing drives complete solvent evaporation, Ostwald ripening, and strain relaxation—collectively yielding large, oriented grains with reduced grain-boundary area, suppressed non-radiative recombination centers (especially undercoordinated Pb²⁺ and I⁻ vacancies), and improved charge-carrier diffusion length. Although no explicit SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in this formulation, the intrinsic defect tolerance of the mixed-cation/halide composition—where Br⁻ substitution at the X-site electronically passivates deep traps by raising the conduction band minimum and narrowing the bandgap distribution, while the A-site entropy stabilizes the perovskite lattice against hydration- and thermal-induced decomposition—functions as a built-in molecular passivation strategy; furthermore, the absence of extrinsic agents ensures unimpeded interfacial energy alignment and eliminates competitive binding or dipole-induced band-bending artifacts that could otherwise compromise charge extraction. Critically, the high VOC of 1.0028 V—approaching the radiative limit for this bandgap—alongside the robust JSC of 19.958 mA/cm² and FF of 79.954% directly reflect the synergistic outcome of suppressed trap-assisted recombination, minimized interfacial energy losses, and homogeneous film morphology, as corroborated by the high PCE of 16.001%.
